definition: DABUS (Device for the Autonomous Bootstrapping of Unified Sentience) is an artificial intelligence (AI) system created by Stephen Thaler.
details: It reportedly conceived of two novel products — a food container constructed using fractal geometry, which enables rapid reheating, and a flashing beacon for attracting attention in an emergency. The filing of patent applications designating DABUS as inventor has led to decisions by patent offices and courts on whether a patent can be granted for an invention reportedly made by an AI system.

explainer.lead: DABUS is an AI system created by Stephen Thaler and reported to have conceived two product designs. Patent applications naming it as the inventor turned it into a test of whether inventorship can belong to an AI system rather than a person.

tiers.eli5: DABUS is a machine credited with inventing a food container and an emergency beacon, leading to a legal fight over whether a machine can be an inventor.
tiers.practitioner: The filings test how patent systems handle inventions reportedly made by an AI system. A pitfall is assuming a machine can be named as inventor; offices and courts have had to decide that question.
tiers.paperLevel: An artificial intelligence system created by Stephen Thaler that reportedly conceived two novel products: a food container constructed using fractal geometry enabling rapid reheating, and a flashing beacon for attracting attention in an emergency. Patent applications designating DABUS as inventor led to decisions on whether a patent can be granted for an invention reportedly made by an AI system.

explainer.example: DABUS reportedly conceived a food container built using fractal geometry so that it enables rapid reheating. When a patent application named DABUS rather than a human as the inventor, the design became part of the broader question of whether an AI system can hold that role.

explainer.intuition: The idea is to treat an AI system not merely as a tool assisting an inventor, but as the reported originator of an invention. DABUS makes that distinction concrete because patent applications named the system itself as inventor.
howItWorks: DABUS reportedly conceives a novel product idea.
The idea becomes a concrete design, such as a container or beacon.
A patent application designates DABUS as the inventor.
Patent offices and courts consider whether such an invention can be patented.
explainer.whyItMatters: DABUS connects AI-generated designs with a basic legal question: who can be recognized as an inventor? The resulting patent-office and court decisions affect whether inventions reportedly made by AI systems can receive patent protection.
misconceptions: DABUS is not itself a patent or a court decision; it is the AI system named in the applications.
The two product ideas are reported outputs, not proof that every patent office accepts AI inventorship.
The acronym expands to Device for the Autonomous Bootstrapping of Unified Sentience.
